sub: Samuel, Saul, David, Solomon · c. 1060–930 BC

stops.before: Hannah weeps for a child in the shrine at Shiloh, is taken for a drunk by the priest, and promises the boy to God before he is born.
stops.watch: Hannah's song (Mary will echo it), the boy hearing his name in the night, the Ark captured by the Philistines and returned on a cart pulled by cows. Then the elders come to old Samuel: 'Give us a king, as all nations have' — and God says, they have not rejected you, they have rejected me.
stops.after: Samuel is sent to anoint a tall young man looking for his father's donkeys.

stops.t: Saul, the king who could not wait
stops.before: Israel gets its king: head and shoulders taller than anyone, modest at first, victorious against the Ammonites.
stops.watch: Two failures that end him: offering the sacrifice himself rather than wait for Samuel, and sparing the Amalekite king and the best sheep. 'To obey is better than sacrifice.' Samuel turns to go, Saul tears his cloak, and the kingdom is torn with it.
stops.after: Samuel goes to Bethlehem with a horn of oil, and a shepherd boy is fetched from the field.

stops.before: 'Man seeth those things that appear, but the Lord beholdeth the heart.' The youngest of eight is anointed in secret, and taken to court to play the harp for the king's black moods.
stops.watch: The giant's armour itemised piece by piece, and the boy who refuses Saul's; five smooth stones; 'the Lord saveth not with sword and spear'. Then Jonathan's love for David, and Saul's jealousy beginning with a song: 'Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands.'
stops.after: The king who anointed him now wants him dead, and David runs.

stops.before: David is a fugitive with six hundred men in the caves of the Judean desert, and Saul hunts him with the army.
stops.watch: Jonathan's arrows and the farewell at the stone; twice David has Saul in his hands, in the cave and in the sleeping camp, and twice will not touch 'the Lord's anointed'. Saul, abandoned by God, consults a witch at Endor and meets the ghost of Samuel. He dies on Mount Gilboa, and Jonathan with him.
stops.after: David's grief is a poem, and then he is king — of Judah only.

stops.before: Seven years of civil war between David in Hebron and Saul's house. Then the tribes come to Hebron and make him king of all Israel.
stops.watch: 'How are the valiant fallen' — David's lament over Saul and Jonathan. The capture of Jerusalem, a neutral city between the tribes, up the water shaft; the Ark brought in with David dancing before it; and chapter 7, the promise that his throne will stand for ever — the root of every hope for a Messiah.
stops.after: At the height of his power, one spring evening on the roof.

stops.before: The army is at war and the king has stayed home. From his roof he sees a woman bathing.
stops.watch: Adultery, then a letter that sends her husband to his death carried by the man himself. Nathan's parable of the one ewe lamb, and the king who condemns himself. David's repentance is Psalm 50 (51 in Hebrew numbering), the Miserere: 'Create a clean heart in me, O God.' The child dies; Solomon is born.
stops.after: 'The sword shall never depart from thy house.' It begins with his own sons.

stops.before: David's eldest son rapes his half-sister Tamar; her brother Absalom kills him for it, flees, returns, and begins to steal the hearts of Israel.
stops.watch: David walking barefoot up the Mount of Olives, weeping, as his son takes his city — the route Jesus will take on another night; the mule, the oak, Absalom hanging by his hair; and the king's cry when they bring the news he asked for.
stops.after: David is old and cold, and two sons want the throne.

stops.before: Before leaving David, sit with the prayers the Bible puts in his mouth — the psalms were sung in his Temple and are still prayed every hour of every day.
stops.watch: Psalm 1, the two ways; 8, the heavens and the son of man; 18 (19), the heavens tell the glory; 21 (22), 'My God, why hast thou forsaken me', prayed on the cross; 22 (23), the shepherd; 26 (27), the Lord is my light; 41 (42), the deer at the stream; 62 (63), thirsting in the desert. The Vulgate numbers run one behind the Hebrew from 10 to 147.
stops.after: David's last act is to name his heir.

stops.t: Give thy servant an understanding heart
stops.before: Adonijah proclaims himself king while David lies dying; Nathan and Bathsheba move fast, and Solomon is anointed at Gihon.
stops.watch: David's last charge, with old scores settled. Then Solomon's dream at Gibeon — offered anything, he asks for wisdom — and the two mothers and one living child: the judgment the whole world remembers.
stops.after: The wise king builds what his father was not allowed to.

stops.before: Cedar from Lebanon, stone dressed at the quarry, 180,000 labourers, seven years. Read chapter 6 with the diagram of the Temple beside it.
stops.watch: The Ark carried in and the cloud filling the house so the priests cannot stand; Solomon's prayer of dedication — 'will God indeed dwell upon earth? the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee' — and the thought that foreigners too will come to pray here.
stops.after: Solomon's wisdom draws the world to Jerusalem, and his wives draw him away.

stops.before: The queen of Sheba comes to test him; gold arrives by the ton; and the tradition gathers three books under his name.
stops.watch: Proverbs 1–3, the fear of the Lord as the beginning of wisdom, and Lady Wisdom calling in the streets; Ecclesiastes' 'vanity of vanities' and its time for everything; the Song of Songs, a love poem the Church reads as Christ and his bride. Then 1 Kings 11: seven hundred wives, other gods, and the sentence — the kingdom will be torn from your son.
stops.after: Solomon dies, and at his son's coronation the north walks out.
